Governmental rationalities and misrecognising human and social conditions in English-in-education policy for individual and social development. • This article provides fresh perspectives in language policy research to critique development in relation to language-in-education policy (LEP) in developing countries. • LEP is a key tool for human capital development. • Sen’s conceptualisation of development is dominant in language policy/education research, but we find this idea problematic as Sen is complicit to human capital theory/ neoliberalism. • Ideological perspective is important to unpack the politics of development discourses and how these are used to govern populations in interested ways. • Misrecognition is central to governing neoliberal citizens and how unequal social struggles over linguistic human capital development are accepted as natural.
